title: Decant + Drip Deployment Notes (personal playbook)
content:
Purpose:
Quick personal playbook for decanting a new model binary and doing a low-risk drip (small continuous ramp) into production. This is me thinking out loud — steps, telemetry to watch, easy rollback triggers, and items to confirm before scheduling. Not a team doc yet; will publish once Sanjay and Eli 👍 the rollback criteria.

Assumptions and constraints:
- New model variant is compatible with current serving runtime (same kv-cache layout and tokenizer).
- We have a dedicated canary queue + ability to tag requests by routing header (x-rw-release).
- Night window: 02:00–06:00 PT is preferred for heavy reroute tests.
- Business stakeholders ok with up to 2% user traffic for a 48h drip if no regressions.

Goals:
- Validate latency distribution and tail behavior under real user mixes.
- Catch quality regressions early via sampling + automatic evals on golden prompts.
- Ensure fallback works and that pinned clients continue to use previous model.

Preflight checklist (must be green before start):
- [ ] Smoke test binary on staging: gen endpoint, embeddings endpoint, streaming. Log success: 100% pass.
- [ ] Run 10k token synthetic throughput test at expected burst size (match busiest client).
- [ ] Confirm KV cache warm path is identical and baseline latency within +15% of prod model.
- [ ] Upload golden prompt set > run auto-eval -> pass score >= baseline_threshold.
- [ ] Routing config ready: header-based split + TTL to avoid sticky cookies.
- [ ] Ops pager rotation confirmed for scheduled window.
- [ ] Rollout plan doc link shared to #releases + product owners.

Drip schedule (example):
- T0 (start): 0.1% global traffic for 1 hour (quick sanity).
- T1: 0.5% for 2 hours (observe).
- T2: 1% for 4 hours.
- T3: 2% steady for 48 hours (if no alerts).
- Ramp step-up only if all green: no >10% relative p95 latency increase, no new 5xx spike >0.5% above baseline, automated quality eval within threshold.

Traffic shaping rules and notes:
- Use header x-rw-release=decant-kb-202403 to pick traffic.
- Exclude heavy API keys used by experiment customers (pin them explicitly).
- Do NOT send traffic from EU regions in first 24h; region-specific infra differences confound results.
- Canary queue should be limited to 8 concurrent requests per worker to avoid queueing effects.

Telemetry and dashboards to watch (alerts should be configured but watch live):
- RPS and error rate (5xx, 4xx spikes) for decant-tagged traffic and baseline.
- Latency p50/p95/p99 and service time breakdown (tokenization, model infer, postproc).
- Token throughput and GPU utilization on the dedicated pool serving the new variant.
- KV cache hit ratio for requests with long histories. Drops here correlate to cold-cache regression.
- Quality eval pipeline: sampled golden prompts + user feedback channel (if enabled).
- Rate-limit / quota enforcement spikes (look for sudden client retries).

Rollback triggers (immediate):
- New 5xx error rate > 0.5% absolute or >3x baseline sustained for 5 minutes.
- p95 latency increase >20% relative to baseline for >= 10 minutes.
- Quality eval degradation: automatic eval score drop >5% absolute vs baseline on golden set.
- Reproducible crash / OOM seen on staging or production.
- Any critical customer incident raised via support channel.

Rollback steps (fast path):
1) Update routing config: remove decant header routing or set header weight to 0% (apply immediately).
2) Verify traffic shift back to baseline model and confirm metrics stabilize.
3) If degraded infra (OOMs), kill offending pods and scale new binary out of pool.
4) Create a rollback postmortem seed note and assign owner (me unless otherwise).

Staging validation snippets (handy commands):
- curl -X POST https://staging.api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -H 'Authorization: Bearer x' -H 'x-rw-release: decant-kb-202403' -d '{"prompt":"short test"}'
- run eval job: ./scripts/run_eval.sh --model decant-kb-202403 --prompts ./golden/prompts.json --output /tmp/eval.json

Observability experiments I want to run during drip:
- Increase sampling of request traces for decant-tagged traffic from 1% to 10% for first 6h.
- Capture full kv-cache state fingerprint (hash length & entries) for a small sample to check compatibility.
- Attach a synthetic background traffic generator that mimics top-3 customers to model tail effects.

Open questions / TODOs:
- Who signs off on extending drip beyond 48h? (cc: product) -> @Eli to confirm SLA window.
- Confirm whether audit logs for private deployments will capture decant header (privacy implication).
- Need a small user cohort for UX sampling (in-product feedback). Will ask PM for opt-in list.
- Decide if we should auto-fork traffic to fallback model on every error spike or only on severe triggers.

Communications plan (short):
- Pre-start: Slack note in #releases, @oncall, and product with link to this doc.
- At each ramp step: brief status update with metrics snapshot.
- On rollback: immediate page + follow-up postmortem stub.

Notes to self:
- Keep the early window conservative; we can always accelerate but not the reverse.
- Document any subtle infra surprises — even if benign — they help later hunts.
- If latency tail climbs at low traffic, focus on cold-cache effects not model perf first.

End of file.
